definitions.explanation: A state that remains unchanged over time, without fluctuation or variation. Often used in scientific and technical contexts to describe systems or processes in equilibrium.

examples.japanese: {定常|ていじょう}{状態|じょうたい}に{達|たっ}する。
{定常|ていじょう}{的|てき}な{運転|うんてん}を{維持|いじ}する。
この{装置|そうち}は{定常|ていじょう}{運転|うんてん}に{入|はい}るまで{数分|すうふん}かかる。
examples.english: This equipment takes several minutes to enter steady-state operation.

notes:
Composed of {定|てい} (fixed, settled) and {常|じょう} (constant, usual). Used primarily as a modifier (with の or {的|てき}) to describe unchanging, stable conditions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {定常|ていじょう}{状態|じょうたい}: steady state
- {定常|ていじょう}{運転|うんてん}: steady-state operation
- {定常|ていじょう}{的|てき}: steady, constant (adjectival form)
- {定常|ていじょう}{波|は}: standing wave (physics)
- {定常|ていじょう}{流|りゅう}: steady flow

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {安定|あんてい}: stable — more common in everyday language, implies being firmly established
- {一定|いってい}: constant / fixed — emphasizes a set, unchanging level
- {恒常|こうじょう}: permanent / constant — emphasizes long-lasting, enduring constancy

REGISTER:
Technical and formal. Frequently used in science, engineering, and economics. In everyday speech, {安定|あんてい} or {一定|いってい} are more natural.
